published_failure_contract: The test module pins jersey-core, jersey-server, jersey-servlet, and jersey-json independently at 1.19. Replacing only core or only server with 1.19.1 creates mixed META-INF/jersey-module-version values. ServiceFinder removes service descriptors from blacklisted Jersey modules whose marker differs from the core marker, so the embedded application cannot complete the WebSocket upgrade and returns HTTP 500; teardown then reports that no connection is open.

source_isolation.evidence: Commit 4416e81f38c76fa3b72179fdf5947a64b3177343 is an ancestor of tag 1.19.1 but not 1.19 and changes ten Jersey module markers from 1.19-SNAPSHOT to 1.20-SNAPSHOT. Maven Central jars preserve those exact values. ServiceFinder lines 225-245 compare each blacklisted module marker with the core marker and remove mismatches. The target pins four sibling Jersey modules separately, so either one-coordinate replacement creates the exact mismatch.

candidate_deduplication.evidence: wordnik/swaggersocket redirects to swagger-api/swagger-socket, both URLs expose byte-identical 34-line remote-ref listings, and all four FSE records name the same module and the same two failure signatures. The core and server interventions share one upstream marker commit and are not counted as separate repository cases.

a1_input.evidence: The FSE package records two exceptions for each coordinate and each repository alias, but omits the exact target revision. The module was introduced once in commit 6dd601941f34257639aab2412cde901d70a25076 and its POM has only one unique blob across all reachable refs, so the dependency layout is recoverable even though the executed commit is not.

target_history.evidence: All 409 commits reachable from branches and pull-request refs and all 519 unique POM blobs were inspected. No POM blob contains Jersey 1.19.1. The JSR-356 client module POM has one unique blob and permanently pins core, server, servlet, and json to 1.19. No maintainer commit upgrades the whole Jersey set or otherwise repairs the published failure.

stop_reason: The source and artifact mechanism is exact, but the complete target history contains no maintainer-authored A2. Upgrading all four Jersey modules now would be a dataset-author repair rather than recovered maintainer behavior.
